sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A stone seated figure with an animal head (ingut figure), explicitly attributed by the museum to Tolai makers of Papua New Guinea — this matches known Tolai carved stone ancestor/spirit figures.

instruments.name: drum; dance equipment
instruments.title: drum; dance equipment
instruments.reason: An hourglass-shaped wooden hand drum with lizard-skin membrane, carved and painted with concentric circles and chevrons, a classic Tolai (Gazelle Peninsula, PNG) garamut-type dance drum form attributed by the museum to Tolai makers.

instruments.name: slit-drum
instruments.title: slit-drum
instruments.reason: A small wooden slit-drum with central tongue and carved handles, a classic form made and used by the Tolai of New Britain for signaling and music; consistent with the museum's stated maker attribution.

masks-ritual.name: dance-mask
masks-ritual.title: dance-mask ('lor')
masks-ritual.reason: This is a composite 'lor' dance mask with carved painted wooden face, fiber beard/hair, feather-edged disk, and a painted wooden peacock figure — a known Tolai ceremonial mask type used in dance/ritual.

masks-ritual.name: dance-wand; bead
masks-ritual.title: dance-wand; bead
masks-ritual.reason: The object is a carved, polychrome wooden dance-wand with a painted human face, fretwork headdress, feather plume, and fibre beard, used in dance/ritual performance — a type of carved ritual object associated with Tolai and neighbouring New Britain peoples.

masks-ritual.name: dance-wand
masks-ritual.title: dance-wand
masks-ritual.reason: A painted wooden dance-wand with feather tuft, a ritual regalia item used in Tolai ceremonial dance, consistent with the museum's attribution to Tolai makers.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden mask with white-painted face, fibre beard, snake crest, and hat covered in red European trade cloth — consistent with Tolai (East New Britain, PNG) ritual masks used in tubuan/dukduk-related ceremonies. The museum directly attributes it to Tolai makers.

masks-ritual.name: Mask
masks-ritual.title: Mask
masks-ritual.reason: The image shows a wooden face mask with simplified carved features and whitish paint, consistent with Tolai masks used in Tubuan/Duk Duk masking traditions of New Britain, PNG; carved wood ritual masks are exactly what this people are known for.

household.name: fishing-net
household.title: fishing-net
household.reason: A seine fishing net with wood floats, stone sinkers, and carved decorated end-floats depicting human and animal figures, explicitly attributed to the Tolai — a plausible and well-documented craft type for this coastal New Britain people.

household.name: adze
household.title: adze
household.reason: A wooden elbow-shaped adze with a shell blade and coconut-fibre lashing, a traditional tool type made and used by the Tolai of New Britain.

household.name: fish-hook
household.title: fish-hook
household.reason: A traditional wooden fish-hook with coconut-fibre binding and snood, a utilitarian item plausible for Tolai material culture from coastal New Britain, Papua New Guinea.
